# Useful AI starts with security .

Before agents run on your machines, the machines have to be safe. Pantry checks everything installed on your Mac or Linux machine, and every repo on it, against open vulnerability and malware data. It reports only what actually applies, names the version that fixes it, and applies the fixes it safely can.

## Install. Scan. Cache. Fix.

One small binary does the whole job on your machine. Only package names and versions ever leave it.

Pantry can read your whole home directory, so every release is signed, hashed and built reproducibly. packslip, GitHub or cosign checks the download before it ever runs.

Pantry takes stock of your runtimes, packages, apps and every repo lockfile, then asks OSV.dev, CISA KEV and endoflife.date about those exact versions. Nothing you have not installed gets reported.

Answers land in a SQLite database on your disk, along with a record of every run. A second scan the same day takes seconds, and you can search the advisories offline.

Preview the plan, then let Pantry run the safe, user-level updates and check again. Anything that needs sudo or a code change is printed for you or your agent to run.

$ mise use -g packslip:github.com/waffuruai/pantry # verifies the signed packslip, then the binaryâs digest $ wpantry version wpantry 0.6.0 (rust, schema 1)

## Secure your system .

Choose how much you want to check yourself. Every route verifies the release before anything runs.

Recommended

### With the install script

Picks the build for your machine, checks it against SHA256SUMS, verifies its signature with packslip, the GitHub CLI or cosign, and installs it to ~/.local/bin.

$ curl -fsSL https://waffuru.ai/pantry/install.sh | sh

Easy updates

### With mise

mise is a more versatile and secure package manager than Homebrew. Install it and turn it on in your shell, then install Pantry. mise reads the releaseâs signed packslip and verifies it against our release workflow before installing anything, then remembers the signer for every update.

- # Install mise and turn it on (zsh, the macOS default) Copy $ curl -fsSL https://mise.run/zsh | sh $ source ~/.zshrc

$ curl -fsSL https://mise.run/zsh | sh $ source ~/.zshrc

- # Or on bash (most Linux) Copy $ curl -fsSL https://mise.run/bash | sh $ source ~/.bashrc

$ curl -fsSL https://mise.run/bash | sh $ source ~/.bashrc

- # Then install Pantry Copy $ mise use -g packslip:github.com/waffuruai/pantry

$ mise use -g packslip:github.com/waffuruai/pantry

By hand

### Verify it yourself

Download the binary, check it against SHA256SUMS and at least one signature (its signed packslip, its GitHub build attestation or its cosign bundle), then install it.

$ ASSET=wpantry-universal-apple-darwin # Linux: wpantry-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl or wpantry-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl $ BASE=https://github.com/waffuruai/pantry/releases/latest/download $ curl -fsSLO "$BASE/$ASSET" -O "$BASE/SHA256SUMS" -O "$BASE/packslip.sigstore.json" $ grep " $ASSET\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - $ packslip verify packslip.sigstore.json --artifact "$ASSET" # or: gh attestation verify "$ASSET" --repo waffuruai/pantry $ install -m 0755 "$ASSET" ~/.local/bin/wpantry

### Other package managers

Homebrew, apt, dnf, pacman and apk packages are on the way. Until then, install with the script or mise above.

$ brew install wpantry # Homebrew, macOS and Linux $ sudo apt install wpantry # Debian and Ubuntu $ sudo dnf install wpantry # Fedora and RHEL $ sudo pacman -S wpantry # Arch Linux $ sudo apk add wpantry # Alpine

### Then scan, see the plan, and write an HTML report.

$ wpantry scan $ wpantry fix --dry-run $ wpantry report --html

## Reports in every format .

Read it in your terminal, share one offline HTML page, or hand JSON to your tools and agents. wpantry report turns the latest scan into any of them, without scanning again.
